features.name: post_placement_slack_multiple_bonus
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Fit slack: remaining room left in a bin after placing the item, scaled by capacity, plus a small bonus for bins whose residual is near a multiple of the item size."""
    rem = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    slack = rem - item
    # normalised post-placement slack (empty bin -> large positive, tight fit -> near 0)
    norm_slack = slack / capacity
    # how close the leftover is to an exact multiple of the item: packing-friendly residuals
    with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
        ratio = rem / item
    frac = ratio - np.floor(ratio)
    near_mult = (np.minimum(frac, 1.0 - frac) < 0.15).astype(float)
    # only reward near-multiples when the bin can actually take the item
    fits = (slack >= 0).astype(float)
    return np.clip(norm_slack, -1.0, 1.0) + 0.2 * near_mult * fits
features.measures: Fit slack: remaining room left in a bin after placing the item, scaled by capacity, plus a small bonus for bins whose residual is near a multiple of the item size.

features.name: exp_fit_matching
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Exponential fit-cost: exp(-remaining/item) per bin, large when remaining just fits the item."""
    total = bins + item
    x = np.clip(total / max(capacity, 1), 0.0, 1.0)
    r = bins / max(capacity, 1)
    it = item / max(capacity, 1)
    # Free space after placing item, shaped by how "matching" the bin is
    room = (bins - item) / max(capacity, 1)
    return np.exp(-np.abs(room) * 4.0) * (1.0 - r) - 0.5
features.measures: Exponential fit-cost: exp(-remaining/item) per bin, large when remaining just fits the item.

features.name: fullness_weighted_slack
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Relative slack of the tightest fit: leftover fraction after placing item, scaled by how tight the bin already is."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    cap = float(capacity)
    it = float(item)
    rem = bins - it
    # fraction of the bin that would remain after placing the item
    frac = np.clip(rem / cap, -1.0, 1.0)
    # how full the bin currently is (before placement), in [0,1]
    fill = np.clip(1.0 - bins / cap, 0.0, 1.0)
    # weight the leftover by current fullness: prefer bins that are already full and still fit
    return frac * (1.0 + fill)
features.measures: Relative slack of the tightest fit: leftover fraction after placing item, scaled by how tight the bin already is.

import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Slack left after placing the item, relative to a scale that grows with how full the bin already is."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    remaining = bins - item
    # how full the bin would be after placement, in [0,1]
    fill = 1.0 - np.clip(remaining / capacity, 0.0, 1.0)
    # penalise tight fits nonlinearly: concave in remaining room, scaled by capacity
    scaled = np.clip(remaining / capacity, 0.0, 1.0)
    return fill * np.sqrt(scaled)

import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Best-fit residual: leftover room after placing the item, normalised by capacity, but squashed so tight fits are separated from merely-fitting bins."""
    residual = (bins - item) / capacity
    # Smooth, monotone squash of the residual: emphasises the difference between
    # near-perfect fits (residual ~ 0) and loose fits (residual large), while
    # staying finite and bounded in [-1, 1].
    return np.tanh(4.0 * residual)

idea.hypothesis: Code Zero is first-fit: it drops each item into the oldest bin that fits, stranding room. Best-fit picks the tightest fitting bin, so leftovers stay small and fewer bins are opened. This is the canonical fix for the 80-95% bins that strand small gaps.
idea.feature: For each candidate bin, leftover = bins - item (elementwise; the last, empty bin gives capacity - item). Return (bins - item) / capacity, one value per candidate. The optimiser will pick the negative sign to prefer the smallest residual.

features.coder_note: This computes `(bins - item) / capacity` elementwise, one value per candidate (the empty bin yields `(capacity - item) / capacity`); the optimiser will choose the negative sign to prefer the tightest fit.
features.measures: Best-fit residual: leftover room after placing the item, normalised by capacity, but squashed so tight fits are separated from merely-fitting bins.

features.name: adaptive_scale_fit
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Exponential fit-cost but with the decay scale set by the bin's current fill level: tight bins demand near-exact fits, empty bins tolerate slack."""
    cap = max(capacity, 1)
    r = bins / cap            # remaining fraction BEFORE placing (empty bin = 1.0)
    it = item / cap
    room = (bins - item) / cap  # leftover fraction after placing
    # scale: how picky the bin is. Full bins (small r) -> sharp; empty bins -> gentle
    scale = 0.5 + 3.5 * (1.0 - r)
    # symmetric in leftover sign, but only reward leftover >= 0 (fits) with more weight
    fit = np.exp(-np.abs(room) * scale)
    # asymmetry: overshoot (shouldn't happen for fitting bins) penalised harder
    asym = np.where(room < 0.0, 0.35, 1.0)
    return np.clip(fit * asym, 0.0, 1.0) * 2.0 - 1.0

name: adaptive_scale_fit
features.measures: Exponential fit-cost but with the decay scale set by the bin's current fill level: tight bins demand near-exact fits, empty bins tolerate slack.

features.name: post_placement_multiple_graded
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Residual-compatibility: after placing the item, how well the leftover room can host future items of the same size — leftover modulo item, graded rather than thresholded, and gated on actually fitting."""
    rem = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    slack = rem - item
    fits = slack >= 0.0

    # Grade how close the post-placement leftover is to an exact multiple of the item,
    # but use the *leftover* (not the pre-placement room) so the signal looks forward.
    safe_item = max(item, 1.0)
    ratio = slack / safe_item
    frac = ratio - np.floor(ratio)
    # triangular closeness to a multiple, in [0,1]: 1 when exact multiple, 0 when half-way
    closeness = 1.0 - 2.0 * np.minimum(frac, 1.0 - frac)

    # Continuous packing-friendliness: leftover near a multiple of the item, and not tiny.
    leftover_frac = np.clip(slack / capacity, -1.0, 1.0)
    # reward residuals that are multiples AND leave enough room for at least one more item
    usable = np.clip(slack / safe_item, 0.0, 1.0)

    score = closeness * usable * fits - 0.5 * leftover_frac
    # The empty (new) bin: leftover = capacity - item, value it by how many items of this size fit.
    return np.clip(score, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Residual-compatibility: after placing the item, how well the leftover room can host future items of the same size — leftover modulo item, graded rather than thresholded, and gated on actually fitting.

features.name: residual_pack_count
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Rank candidates by how many future items of the observed size scale would still fit: estimate of remaining capacity fragmentation."""
    cap = max(capacity, 1)
    item_f = item / cap
    rem = bins / cap
    # two natural scales for future items: mean training size (~0.3*cap) and a small tail (~0.1*cap)
    s1 = 0.30
    s2 = 0.10
    # how many s1-sized and s2-sized items could still go into each bin (continuous relaxation)
    n1 = np.maximum(rem - item_f + item_f, 0.0)  # placeholder to avoid unused warning
    room = np.maximum(rem - item_f, 0.0)
    cnt = room / s1 + room / s2
    # reward bins whose leftover cleanly packs many small items (smooth, bounded)
    val = np.tanh(cnt) - 0.3
    # empty bin gets a fixed neutral value so it isn't overly favoured or punished
    val[-1] = np.tanh((1.0 - item_f) / s1 + (1.0 - item_f) / s2) - 0.3
    return val
features.measures: Rank candidates by how many future items of the observed size scale would still fit: estimate of remaining capacity fragmentation.

features.name: leftover_rank_vs_bins
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Number of already-open bins this candidate's leftover could still absorb if it were the only remaining item, plus 1."""
    k = len(bins)
    leftover = bins - item
    # how many of the OTHER open bins (excluding the new bin) are at least as empty as this leftover
    # measure: relative rank of this bin's post-placement room against the distribution of all bins
    c = max(capacity, 1)
    lf = np.clip(leftover / c, -1.0, 1.0)
    # count, as a fraction of k, how many bins have room below this candidate's leftover
    # (vectorised pairwise comparison)
    diff = lf[None, :] - lf[:, None]          # (k, k): other - self
    frac_below = (diff > 0).sum(axis=1) / max(k - 1, 1)
    # also give new bin a distinct nudge based on how full the system already is
    total_room = bins.sum() / c
    open_room = (bins[:-1].sum() / c) if k > 1 else 0.0
    is_new = np.zeros(k)
    is_new[-1] = 1.0
    return np.tanh(3.0 * (frac_below - 0.5)) + 0.3 * is_new * np.tanh(open_room - total_room + item / c)
features.measures: Number of already-open bins this candidate's leftover could still absorb if it were the only remaining item, plus 1.

features.name: adaptive_headroom_band
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Asymmetric Gaussian band on leftover headroom: peak shifts toward 0.5 for small items and toward 0.0 for large ones, width scales with item size."""
    leftover = (bins - item) / capacity
    r = item / capacity
    # Peak: large items want near-exact fits (peak -> 0), small items spread out (peak -> ~0.5)
    peak = 0.5 * (1.0 - r) ** 1.5
    # Width: narrow for large items (exact fits matter), wide for small items
    width = 0.10 + 0.25 * (1.0 - r)
    return np.exp(-((leftover - peak) ** 2) / (2.0 * width ** 2 + 1e-9)) - 0.5
features.measures: Asymmetric Gaussian band on leftover headroom: peak shifts toward 0.5 for small items and toward 0.0 for large ones, width scales with item size.

features.name: multiscale_fit_smoothing
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Fit-cost smoothing over neighboring item scales: exp(-|bins - s|/capacity) averaged over item sizes s near the arriving item, weighted by how empty the bin is."""
    cap = max(capacity, 1)
    r = bins / cap
    it = item / cap
    # A small band of plausible next-item scales around the arriving item's size.
    scales = np.array([0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.25, 1.6]) * it  # fractions of the current item
    # Residual after placing a hypothetical item of each scale, in capacity units.
    # bins shape (k,), scales shape (s,) -> residuals (k, s)
    resid = (bins[:, None] - (scales[None, :] * cap)) / cap
    # Scale-dependent tolerance: bigger items demand tighter matching.
    width = 0.15 + 0.5 * scales[None, :]
    fit = np.exp(-np.abs(resid) / width)
    # Weight each hypothetical scale by the size of the item being imagined (large items matter more).
    w = scales / scales.sum()
    match = (fit * w[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
    # Reward emptier bins (more room to absorb mismatch), centre around 0.
    return match * (1.0 - r) - 0.5
features.measures: Fit-cost smoothing over neighboring item scales: exp(-|bins - s|/capacity) averaged over item sizes s near the arriving item, weighted by how empty the bin is.

import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Interaction: how much of the bin's current fill is 'protected' by being a tight fit for this item."""
    cap = max(capacity, 1)
    # current fill fraction of each bin (before placing)
    fill = 1.0 - bins / cap
    # how tightly the item fits relative to remaining room: 1 when exact, ->0 when roomy
    tight = item / np.maximum(bins, 1e-9)
    tight = np.clip(tight, 0.0, 1.0)
    # interaction: reward bins that are already fairly full AND that the item nearly exactly fills
    return (2.0 * fill - 1.0) * tight

features.name: post_placement_decisiveness
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Negative entropy of the post-placement room distribution: rewards bins whose fill state (full/empty) is decisive, punishes mediocre middle states."""
    k = len(bins)
    post = bins - item
    # Normalised post-placement room for real bins; the empty bin is special-cased.
    r = np.clip(post / max(capacity, 1), 0.0, 1.0)
    # Entropy-like "middle-ness": peaks at r=0.5, zero at extremes (parabolic).
    mid = 4.0 * r * (1.0 - r)          # 0 at full/empty, 1 at half-full
    # How decisive the bin's state is: full-ish or empty-ish is good, half-full is bad.
    val = 1.0 - 2.0 * mid              # +1 decisive, -1 mediocre
    # The brand-new empty bin is always maximally decisive (r = 1 - item/cap is high room).
    val[-1] = 1.0
    # Also weight by whether this item actually leaves a decisive state, not the pre-state.
    return val
features.measures: Negative entropy of the post-placement room distribution: rewards bins whose fill state (full/empty) is decisive, punishes mediocre middle states.

import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Blend of tight-fit band (small items) and headroom (large items), weighted by item/capacity."""
    cap = max(capacity, 1)
    it = item / cap
    room = (bins - item) / cap
    tight = np.exp(-np.abs(room) * 4.0) - 0.5
    head = np.clip(room, -1.0, 1.0)
    return (1.0 - it) * tight + it * head

import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Asymmetric exponential fit-cost: penalise leaving too much room far more than packing too tight, using a scale set by the item's own size."""
    cap = max(capacity, 1)
    room = (bins - item) / cap            # leftover after placing; negative only if it doesn't fit (shouldn't happen)
    it = item / cap
    # Asymmetric decay: over-spacious placements decay with the item's own footprint scale,
    # tight/negative leftovers decay much faster (we don't want to shave bins to the bone).
    scale = np.clip(it, 0.05, 1.0)
    over = np.maximum(room, 0.0)
    under = np.maximum(-room, 0.0)
    score = np.exp(-over / scale) - np.exp(-under / (0.25 * scale))
    return score - 0.5
features.measures: Asymmetric exponential fit-cost: penalise leaving too much room far more than packing too tight, using a scale set by the item's own size.

import numpy as np
import math

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Fit-cost that compares post-placement leftover against the item itself: exp(-leftover/item) but only for bins that already hold something, plus a bonus for the empty bin scaled by how poorly it fits."""
    it = max(item, 1)
    r = bins / max(capacity, 1)
    leftover = bins - item
    # Negative room means the item does not fit; the empty bin always fits.
    fits = leftover >= 0
    # Asymmetric shape: tight fits rewarded, but with a floor so leftover=0 is not a singularity
    ratio = np.where(fits, leftover / it, 1.0)
    tight = np.exp(-ratio * 2.0) - 0.5
    # Penalise bins that are nearly full but not matching (their leftover is small yet the bin is crowded)
    crowded = np.exp(-np.abs(r - 0.5) * 6.0)
    # Empty bin (last, r == 1.0) gets a flatter response relying on how big the item is
    empty = (r > 0.999).astype(float)
    empty_bonus = empty * (0.5 - item / max(capacity, 1))
    return tight * (1.0 - 0.5 * crowded) + empty_bonus
features.measures: Fit-cost that compares post-placement leftover against the item itself: exp(-leftover/item) but only for bins that already hold something, plus a bonus for the empty bin scaled by how poorly it fits.

import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Tight-fit vs pairing resonance: reward leftovers near 0 or near a multiple of the item size, with width scaled by item size."""
    L = (bins - item) / capacity
    it = item / capacity
    # width of the pairing resonance grows with the item (small items pair loosely, large items sharply)
    w = 0.04 + 0.6 * it
    # resonance at leftover ~ m*item for m = 0,1,2 (exact, pair, triple)
    res = np.zeros_like(L)
    for m in range(3):
        mu = m * it
        width = (0.05 if m == 0 else w)
        amp = 1.0 if m == 0 else (0.8 if m == 1 else 0.5)
        res = np.maximum(res, amp * np.exp(-0.5 * ((L - mu) / width) ** 2))
    # scale resonance by how well the bin can host this item at all
    host = np.clip((bins - item) / max(capacity, 1) + 1.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    return res * host - 0.35

    cap = max(capacity, 1)

features.name: dead_zone_signed_penalty
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Signed non-monotone score: -1 where the item doesn't fit, else max(exact-fill Gaussian, twin-reserve ramp) - 0.45."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    item = float(item)
    cap = float(capacity)

    Lc = (bins - item) / cap
    exact = np.exp(-((Lc / 0.07) ** 2))

    leftover = bins - item
    ratio = leftover / max(item, 1.0)
    res = np.clip((ratio - 1.0) / 0.8, 0.0, 1.0)

    val = np.maximum(exact, res) - 0.45
    return np.where(bins < item, -1.0, val)

idea.hypothesis: The large family wastes room in bins whose post-placement leftover is positive but smaller than the item (19 nearly-empty and many 95-98% bins, 45 singletons). A signed non-monotone score - high on exact fits, high once the leftover can host a twin, flat and negative in between - should convert dead leftovers into either sealed bins or usable reserves. This isolates the dead zone as a penalty rather than the narrow reward bump f037 tried.
idea.feature: Lc=(bins-item)/capacity; exact=exp(-(Lc/0.07)^2) (peak 1 at exact fill); res=clip(((bins-item)/max(item,1)-1.0)/0.8,0,1) (0 while leftover<=item, 1 at leftover>=1.8*item); val=maximum(exact,res)-0.45; return -1.0 where bins<item, val otherwise.
idea.lesson: f037 (a positive Gaussian bump at leftover 8%) was rejected on the probe; the dead zone should be punished and the two outside regions rewarded, not the middle rewarded.

features.measures: Signed non-monotone score: -1 where the item doesn't fit, else max(exact-fill Gaussian, twin-reserve ramp) - 0.45.

features.name: new_bin_opportunity_cost
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(item, bins, capacity):
    """Zero for every real open bin; for the trailing empty bin, minus the best exp(-(remaining-item)/item) fit quality among the real bins."""
    bins = np.asarray(bins, dtype=float)
    k = bins.shape[0]
    i = max(float(item), 1.0)
    q = np.where(bins >= item, np.exp(-np.clip((bins - item) / i, 0.0, 50.0)), 0.0)
    b = float(np.max(q[:-1])) if k > 1 else 0.0
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    out[-1] = -b
    return out

idea.hypothesis: Large opens 14 bins above the provable minimum and 19 bins end under half full: opening a fresh bin is currently a fixed-threshold decision. Scoring the empty bin by the negative of the best fit quality available among the real bins makes it pay the opportunity cost of the best alternative it would displace, so a fresh bin is only opened when no real bin offers a genuinely good fit.
idea.feature: i=max(item,1); q=where(bins>=item, exp(-clip((bins-item)/i,0,50)), 0.0); b=max(q[:-1]) if k>1 else 0 (best quality among the real open bins, excluding the trailing empty bin); return a zero vector with the last entry set to -b (all real bins 0, empty bin -b).
idea.lesson: f036 (worst-fit when no exact fit, large items only) was rejected by the probe: changing the fit direction is not the lever, pricing the new-bin decision is.

features.measures: Zero for every real open bin; for the trailing empty bin, minus the best exp(-(remaining-item)/item) fit quality among the real bins.

features.name: age_tiebreak_ramp

idea.hypothesis: f035's exact and twin peaks create many exact ties, and ties currently go to the oldest bin, so placements drift and freshly opened bins are starved into singletons. A pure age feature, orthogonal to every leftover-based feature in the policy, tests whether the tie-break order matters at all; a fitted non-zero weight means age carries real information.
idea.feature: k=len(bins); return linspace(-1.0, 1.0, k): oldest bin -1, newest (the empty bin, always last) +1, linear in between; zeros if k==1.
idea.lesson: f013 rank-vs-bins sits in the f002 duplicate group; age (position in the bins array) is the only quantity the policy never sees and exact/twin peaks make ties common.

features.coder_note: This computes a pure age tie-break ramp: `-1` for the oldest candidate bin, `+1` for the newest (the always-last empty bin), evenly spaced in between, and `0` when there is only one candidate. I read "newest" as the last entry of `bins`, which the problem guarantees is the brand-new empty bin.
features.measures: Age ramp weighted by how much room the bin has left: (2*rank/(k-1)-1) * (remaining/capacity).

nodes.title: large-item headroom
nodes.description: Prefer bins whose leftover after placement stays above a threshold (e.g. half capacity) so future large items still fit.

nodes.title: wide find: post_placement_slack_multiple_bonus
nodes.description: Fit slack: remaining room left in a bin after placing the item, scaled by capacity, plus a small bonus for bins whose residual is near a multiple of the item size.

nodes.title: exact-fit vs hole
nodes.description: Two-sided score: reward near-exact post-placement fits but also reward leaving a leftover large enough for a typical future item, penalising the middle band.

nodes.title: item-size-relative residual
nodes.description: Measure leftover after placement relative to the arriving item's size rather than capacity, so the same bin looks tight for big items and roomy for small ones.

nodes.title: size-conditional fit
nodes.description: Switch between tight-fit and headroom preference depending on how large the arriving item is relative to capacity.

nodes.title: pre-placement room
nodes.description: Score candidates by their room before placement (not after), so the item's own size does not dominate the ordering.

nodes.title: adaptive headroom band
nodes.description: Headroom band whose peak and width shift with item size, so large items demand more leftover than small ones.

nodes.title: regime-conditional fit cost
nodes.description: Exponential fit cost whose decay scale adapts to the global fill pressure (mean bin fill), tightening as bins fill up.

nodes.title: two-peak headroom band
nodes.description: Headroom band with two peaks: one at exact fit (0) and one at half-capacity, so both tight packing and large-hole preservation are rewarded.

nodes.title: twin-reserve dead-zone matching
nodes.description: Non-monotone item-relative score: reward post-placement leftover ~0 (exact fit) and leftover >= item (room for a twin), penalise the dead zone 0 < leftover < item where no same-size item can follow.

nodes.title: opportunity-cost new-bin penalty
nodes.description: Score the empty bin by the negative of the best fit quality available among existing bins, so opening a new bin is penalised in proportion to how good the available fits are.
